templates.title: 555 LED blinker
templates.summary: The board from the home page: a USB-C powered 555 timer that blinks an LED about once a second.
templates.detail: A classic first circuit with everything a real board has: a connector, a timer chip, the resistors and capacitors that set its rate, a ground pour and mounting holes. The guided first project uses this board.

templates.title: USB-C 3.3 V regulator
templates.summary: A USB-C power inlet, an AMS1117-3.3 linear regulator and a power LED, broken out to a three-pin header.
templates.detail: The supply most small boards start from: 5 V from any USB-C charger, regulated down to 3.3 V at up to 800 mA. Copy the regulator block into your own design, or swap the header for whatever you are powering.

templates.title: I2C temperature sensor breakout
templates.summary: An LM75B temperature sensor with its decoupling capacitor and bus pull-ups on a five-pin header.
templates.detail: The shape of nearly every sensor breakout: one chip, one capacitor, pull-ups on the bus, and a header. Replace the LM75B with the part you need and keep the rest. The address pins are tied low, so the sensor answers at 0x48.

templates.title: ATtiny85 development board
templates.summary: An ATtiny85 with a programming header, a reset button, an LED and two spare pins on a header.
templates.detail: A complete small microcontroller board: decoupling, reset with a pull-up and a button, the six-pin ISP header every AVR programmer plugs into, an LED on PB3 and a header for PB3, PB4 and power. A good first board to build and to grow.
